simple: the few numbers that describe where the robot is and how it is moving right now.
analogy: Nia's place on the river road and her speed.
precise: the set of variables whose present values, together with the future inputs, determine the future behaviour; for a robot in a corridor, its position; for a robot on a floor, (x, y, θ), possibly with velocities and sensor biases. Same idea as MA301 F0-67.
source: D1 of F9-30 ("Probabilistic Robotics") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: what the robot thinks about where it is: every possible place, with a probability for each.
analogy: Nia's "somewhere around the boathouse, give or take a bit".
precise: the probability distribution of the state x_t given all measurements z_1:t and controls u_1:t so far, written bel(x_t) = p(x_t | z_1:t, u_1:t).
source: D1 of F9-30 ("Probabilistic Robotics") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: how spread out the belief is.
analogy: the size of Nia's "give or take".
precise: a measure of the spread of the belief, for example its variance (one state variable) or its covariance matrix (several); for beliefs with several peaks, no single number describes it fully.
source: D1 of F9-30 ("Probabilistic Robotics") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: cut the world into cells and store one probability per cell.
analogy: numbering the stretches of the river road and saying how likely each one is.
precise: a discrete approximation of the belief by the probability mass in each cell of a fixed partition of the state space; the masses are non-negative and sum to 1.
source: D1 of F9-30 ("Probabilistic Robotics") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: describe the belief by a best guess and a spread, assuming the bell shape.
analogy: "the boathouse, plus or minus fifty metres".
precise: a belief of the form N(μ, Σ), fully described by its mean vector μ and covariance matrix Σ; it has exactly one peak.
source: D1 of F9-30 ("Probabilistic Robotics") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: many sample guesses of the state; where the guesses crowd, the robot is likely to be.
analogy: a crowd of imaginary Nias, each riding with slightly different timing.
precise: a set of samples x^[1], …, x^[M] (optionally with weights) whose distribution approximates the belief; used by the particle filter (F9-36).
source: D1 of F9-30 ("Probabilistic Robotics") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: where the robot might end up when it is told to move.
analogy: "one more minute of pedalling: probably one block further, maybe a little less or more".
precise: the conditional distribution p(x_t | u_t, x_t−1) of the new state given the control and the previous state.
source: D1 of F9-31 ("Probabilistic Robotics") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: how likely each reading is in each state.
analogy: "at a shop I almost always see a lit window; at a hedge I rarely think I do".
precise: the conditional distribution p(z_t | x_t); viewed as a function of x_t for the reading actually received it is the likelihood (F0-61).
source: D1 of F9-31 ("Probabilistic Robotics") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: if you know the present state exactly, the past tells you nothing more about the future.
analogy: knowing exactly where he is, Oskar does not need to remember which windows he passed.
precise: the state x_t is complete: p(x_t | x_0:t−1, z_1:t−1, u_1:t) = p(x_t | x_t−1, u_t) and p(z_t | x_0:t, z_1:t−1, u_1:t) = p(z_t | x_t).
source: D1 of F9-31 ("Probabilistic Robotics") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the number you divide by so that the probabilities add up to 1 again.
analogy: after crossing out the guesses that do not fit, sharing out "all of the certainty" among those left.
precise: η = 1 / Σ_x p(z_t | x) bel‾(x), the reciprocal of the probability of the reading under the prediction.
source: D1 of F9-31 ("Probabilistic Robotics") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: finding where you are with no idea at the start, versus keeping track when you already roughly know.
analogy: Oskar's first ride in the dark versus his hundredth.
precise: global localisation starts from a uniform (or very wide) belief and must cope with several peaks; position tracking starts from a narrow belief and keeps it narrow. The kidnapped-robot problem is global localisation that begins after the robot was moved without being told.
source: D1 of F9-31 ("Probabilistic Robotics") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a recipe that keeps a best guess and how unsure it is, moves both with the robot, and blends in each new reading according to how trustworthy it is.
analogy: combining two friends' guesses, trusting the more reliable one more (registered F9 analogy).
precise: the Bayes filter for a linear system with Gaussian noise; the belief stays Gaussian and is carried as a mean and a variance (covariance matrix in several dimensions). The filter is named after R. E. Kalman, whose 1960 paper on linear filtering is the historical original.
source: D1 of F9-32 ("Probabilistic Robotics") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: how much doubt one prediction step adds.
analogy: how wrong Lin's wheel count can become in one minute of riding.
precise: the variance (covariance) of the random error added by the motion model in one step.
source: D1 of F9-32 ("Probabilistic Robotics") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: how much a single reading can be off.
analogy: Farah's "give or take 300 metres".
precise: the variance (covariance) of the measurement error, assumed zero-mean, Gaussian and independent between readings; measured, for example, from readings at a known position (F0-62).
source: D1 of F9-32 ("Probabilistic Robotics") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the share of the surprise that the filter believes.
analogy: how far towards Farah's number the pair moves (0 = ignore her, 1 = take her number).
precise: in one dimension K = P / (P + R), between 0 and 1; the update is x ← x + K (z − x).
source: D1 of F9-32 ("Probabilistic Robotics") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: how much the reading surprised the filter.
analogy: the 0.6 km between Lin's 10.0 and Farah's 10.6.
precise: the difference y = z − x̂^− between the reading and its prediction, with predicted variance S = P^− + R; for a correct filter the innovations are zero-mean, have variance S and are uncorrelated in time.
source: D1 of F9-32 ("Probabilistic Robotics") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the surprise measured in units of "how surprised the filter expected to be".
analogy: Farah's 0.6 km surprise divided by the pair's combined "give or take".
precise: ν = y² / S; for a consistent filter with one measurement its mean is 1. A mean far above 1 means the filter claims too little uncertainty (overconfident).
source: W1 of F9-32 (the chapter's own derivation and lab runs) — pending verification

simple: the list of numbers the filter estimates.
analogy: "where we are and how fast we go" on the bicycle trip.
precise: a column vector x with n entries chosen so that the next state depends only on the current state, the inputs and fresh noise (the state of a dynamic system, F0-67); in this chapter x = [position, velocity]^T.
source: D1 of F9-33 ("Probabilistic Robotics") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the rule that moves the state one step forward.
analogy: "in ten minutes at 9 km/h we move 1.5 km further, and our speed stays the same".
precise: the n × n matrix of the linear motion model x_k = F x_k−1 + B u_k + w_k; for constant velocity, F = [[1, Δt], [0, 1]].
source: D1 of F9-33 ("Probabilistic Robotics") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the rule that says what a sensor would read for a given state.
analogy: the kilometre post shows position, never speed.
precise: the m × n matrix of the linear measurement model z_k = H x_k + v_k; for a position sensor, H = [1, 0].
source: D1 of F9-33 ("Probabilistic Robotics") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: how large the filter expects the next surprise to be.
analogy: how far the next post may plausibly differ from where Farah expects it.
precise: S = H P^− H^T + R, an m × m matrix; it replaces P^− + R of F9-32.
source: D1 of F9-33 ("Probabilistic Robotics") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a longer but safer way to write the covariance update.
analogy: checking a sum by adding the column twice in different orders.
precise: P = (I − KH) P^− (I − KH)^T + K R K^T; algebraically equal to (I − KH) P^− for the optimal K, but it keeps P symmetric and positive semidefinite under rounding errors.
source: D1 of F9-33 ("Probabilistic Robotics") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the real error measured in units of the error the filter claims.
analogy: how far off Farah's guess of position and speed really was, compared with her own "give or take".
precise: ε = e^T P^−1 e with e = x̂ − x_true; needs ground truth; its mean is n (the number of states) for a consistent filter.
source: W1 of F9-33 (the chapter's own derivation and lab runs) — pending verification

simple: a Kalman filter for curved models, which treats each curve as straight near the current guess.
analogy: a bend in the road looks straight for the next few metres.
precise: predicts the mean with the non-linear models g and h, and the covariance with their Jacobians evaluated at the current estimate; an approximation, not an optimal filter.
source: D1 of F9-34 ("Probabilistic Robotics") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a table of how much each output changes when each input changes a little.
analogy: how much the lighthouse angle changes if Lin is one metre further left.
precise: the matrix of first partial derivatives, J_ij = ∂f_i/∂x_j; it is the linear approximation of f near a point (F0-64).
source: D3 of F9-34 ("Introduction to Probability") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a robot that drives forward and turns, but never slides sideways.
analogy: a bicycle on dry ground.
precise: x' = x + v Δt cos θ, y' = y + v Δt sin θ, θ' = θ + ω Δt, with speed v and turn rate ω from odometry; a common model for differential-drive robots.
source: D2 of F9-34 ("Modern Robotics") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: "the landmark is this far away, at this angle from where I am facing".
analogy: Lin's glance at the lighthouse.
precise: h(s) = [√(Δx² + Δy²), atan2(Δy, Δx) − θ] with Δx = l_x − x, Δy = l_y − y.
source: D1 of F9-34 ("Probabilistic Robotics") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: bringing an angle back into one turn, so that "359°" and "−1°" are the same.
analogy: a clock hand at 11:59 is one minute from 12:00, not eleven hours.
precise: mapping an angle to (−π, π] by adding or subtracting 2π; needed for every heading and every angle difference, including innovations.
source: W1 of F9-34 (the chapter's own derivation and lab runs) — pending verification

simple: a fixed, recognisable thing whose position on the map is known.
analogy: the lighthouse.
precise: a feature with known map coordinates and (in this chapter) a known identity in each reading; recognising which landmark was seen is the data-association problem.
source: D1 of F9-34 ("Probabilistic Robotics") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: combining several sensors so that each covers the others' weaknesses.
analogy: riding by both the wheel count and the inner ear.
precise: estimating one state from several measurement models in one filter, each weighted by its noise covariance; the result is better than any single sensor only if the models (including biases and outliers) are right.
source: D1 of F9-35 ("Probabilistic Robotics") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: adding a sensor's error to the list of things the filter estimates.
analogy: Farah learning how much her inner ear leans.
precise: extending the state vector with parameters such as a bias b, given a motion model (here a slow random walk) and appearing in the measurement model (here z_gyro = ω + b + noise).
source: D1 of F9-35 ("Probabilistic Robotics") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a rule that throws away a reading that is far too surprising.
analogy: when the wheels report a sharp turn the ear never felt, ignore the wheels.
precise: skipping an update when its NIS y²/S exceeds a threshold; for one measurement and a consistent filter, P(NIS > 9) = 0.0027 (run R4).
source: D1 of F9-35 ("Probabilistic Robotics") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a wheel turning without moving the robot the same distance.
analogy: a tyre spinning on gravel.
precise: a violation of the rolling-without-slipping assumption of odometry; it produces large, short, non-Gaussian errors in the odometry speed and turn rate.
source: D1 of F9-35 ("Probabilistic Robotics") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a self-contained program that receives sensor messages and publishes where the robot is and how sure it is.
analogy: the part of Farah's brain that keeps track of where she is from all her senses.
precise: a software component with message inputs (odometry, IMU, landmark readings), an internal filter, time-stamp handling and a pose-with-covariance output at a fixed rate; the RB302 project and an MP6 component.
source: W1 of F9-35 (the chapter's own derivation and lab runs) — pending verification

simple: a Bayes filter whose belief is a crowd of guesses.
analogy: the cycling club spread along the ring.
precise: a sequential Monte Carlo implementation of the Bayes filter: the belief is approximated by N samples (particles) with weights; prediction samples each particle from the motion model, the update multiplies weights by the measurement likelihood, and resampling replaces low-weight particles by copies of high-weight ones. Used for robot localisation under the name Monte Carlo localisation.
source: D1 of F9-36 ("Probabilistic Robotics") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: how well one guess fits the readings.
analogy: how loudly a rider shouts "that fits me!".
precise: a non-negative number w_i attached to particle i, multiplied by p(z | x_i) at each update and normalised to sum to 1.
source: D1 of F9-36 ("Probabilistic Robotics") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: copying good guesses and dropping poor ones.
analogy: the club's reshuffle.
precise: drawing N new particles from the current ones with probability proportional to weight and resetting the weights to 1/N; systematic (low-variance) resampling uses one random offset and N equally spaced pointers.
source: D1 of F9-36 ("Probabilistic Robotics") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: how many of the guesses are really doing work.
analogy: if only three riders are shouting, the club is effectively three riders.
precise: ESS = 1/Σw_i²: N for equal weights, 1 when one particle holds all the weight; a common rule resamples when ESS < N/2.
source: W1 of F9-36 (the chapter's own derivation and lab runs) — pending verification

simple: the crowd has collapsed into a few clones, so no guess is near the truth any more.
analogy: the whole club standing in one spot, sure of itself, while Lin is elsewhere.
precise: loss of diversity in the particle set through repeated resampling, especially without motion noise; the filter can no longer represent hypotheses away from its clones and cannot recover.
source: D1 of F9-36 ("Probabilistic Robotics") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the robot is picked up and put somewhere else without being told.
analogy: Lin is driven to another part of the ring in a van.
precise: a test of whether a localisation filter can recover from a belief that is confidently wrong; it requires the filter to keep some probability everywhere.
source: D1 of F9-36 ("Probabilistic Robotics") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)
